item.title: Dispersal order issued in Sutton Bridge following anti-social behaviour
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Dispersal order issued in Sutton Bridge following anti-social behaviour
A dispersal order is now in effect for Sutton Bridge following reports of anti-social behaviour and criminal offences. Inspector Paul Smith has authorised the measure for Bridge Road and all adjoining streets, including the Sutton Bridge Memorial Park. The order began at 8am this morning, Friday, October 10, and will remain in place until 8am on Monday, October 12.
Police have received reports of property damage, including doors being kicked and items being thrown at residents. Officers have been granted powers to remove individuals from the area if they are suspected of causing harassment or distress. Additional police resources have been deployed to the village, and authorities are urging parents to speak with their children regarding these incidents.

item.title: South Wootton pub closes just five months after reopening
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
South Wootton pub closes just five months after reopening
The Swan in South Wootton, near King’s Lynn, has closed its doors once again. Publicans Jay Hudson and Maggie Hodgkiss, who took over the venue in May, announced the decision on social media yesterday. The pair cited the current economic climate and unforeseen circumstances as the reasons for the closure, describing the situation as incredibly challenging.
The pub, located on Nursery Lane, had undergone a refresh of its interior and beer garden prior to the couple's arrival. The operator, Stonegate Group, has now listed the historic venue for rent. The publicans have thanked their staff and customers for their support during their time at the pub.

item.title: Admissions remain suspended at King’s Lynn mental health ward
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Admissions remain suspended at King’s Lynn mental health ward
Admissions to the Samphire Ward at Chatterton House in King’s Lynn remain temporarily paused. The Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust says the suspension is based on quality and safety grounds and will continue for the coming months. No date has been set for the ward to reopen to new patients.
The trust confirms that Chatterton House remains open, and anyone requiring inpatient care will be offered a bed elsewhere within the organisation. The pause is part of a wider transformation programme for mental health services across the region, which includes plans for a new neighbourhood mental health centre in King’s Lynn. Officials state that patient and staff safety remains their highest priority while this work is completed.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/admissions-to-mental-health-ward-remain-paused-with-no-dat-9486208/

item.title: Overnight roadworks planned for Hardwick Roundabout
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Overnight roadworks planned for Hardwick Roundabout
Motorists in King’s Lynn are being warned of upcoming disruption as survey work begins at the Hardwick Roundabout. Starting Monday, October 12, Norfolk County Council will implement overnight lane closures and traffic light controls on sections of the A47 and A10. These measures are scheduled between 8pm and 6am to minimise impact on daytime traffic.
The surveys are part of the West Winch Housing Access Road project and are expected to last until the end of November, though some work may extend into early December. Contractors will be assessing road surfaces and drainage. While the majority of the project is scheduled for overnight, officials have confirmed that any particularly noisy tasks will be completed before 11pm.

A King’s Lynn charity has hosted a social evening to help combat isolation among the local Armed Forces community. Beneficiaries of The Bridge for Heroes enjoyed a trip to the Strikes bowling alley in Gaywood, followed by a fish and chip supper at the charity’s South Clough Lane centre.
The outing was made possible through funding from Project Out and About Norfolk, which is supported by the Norfolk Community Foundation. Members of the Armed Forces community interested in learning more about these services can contact The Bridge for Heroes on 01553 760230.

item.title: Ethical coffee chain set to open in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Ethical coffee chain set to open in King’s Lynn
A new organic coffee shop is coming to King’s Lynn. Esquires, The Organic Coffee Company, is planning to move into the former Coneys, Burton, and Dorothy Perkins premises at 98 to 99 High Street. The site has remained vacant since February, but workmen have been spotted inside the building this week.
West Norfolk Council has granted planning permission for the chain to install its signage at the location. The application was submitted by brand project manager Ash Flawn. Esquires, which originated in Canada, recently opened another franchise in Swaffham. The company has not yet confirmed an official opening date for the new King’s Lynn branch.

Plans for a new housing development in Long Sutton have been turned down by the local council. The proposal sought permission to build more than 120 homes in the area. South Holland District Council has rejected the application, meaning the project will not proceed as planned.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Planning decision for Brewin Avenue to go to committee
A planning application for Brewin Avenue in March is set to be decided by a committee. This follows objections from both local planning officers and the town of March, who have both advised against the proposal. Despite these recommendations, the application will now be reviewed by the Fenland District Council planning committee for a final decision.
